issue.title: Update: [HTTP Security Response Headers Cheat Sheet]
issue.body:
## What is missing or needs to be updated?

The [[HTTP Headers Cheat Sheet](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/HTTP_Headers_Cheat_Sheet.html#access-control-allow-origin)](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/HTTP_Headers_Cheat_Sheet.html#access-control-allow-origin) currently documents the `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` response header but does not mention the closely related `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials` header.

`Access-Control-Allow-Credentials` is an important part of CORS configuration when cross-origin requests require credentials such as cookies.

## How should this be resolved?

Add a small subsection about `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials` under the existing `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` section.

The subsection should cover:

- Its purpose and functionality in credentialed CORS requests.
- Its valid value (`true`) and when the header should be omitted.
- Its relationship with `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`.
- The restriction that wildcard origins (`*`) cannot be used with credentialed CORS responses.
- The security implications of allowing credentials for untrusted origins.
- A recommendation to allow credentials only for explicitly trusted origins.

**References:**
- [[MDN – Access-Control-Allow-Credentials](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Headers/Access-Control-Allow-Credentials)](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Headers/Access-Control-Allow-Credentials)
- [[MDN – Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS)](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Guides/CORS)](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Guides/CORS)
- [[WHATWG Fetch Standard](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/)](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/)

<!-- Thank you again for your contribution -->

comments.body:
I would like to take this one if it is still open. Access-Control-Allow-Credentials is missing from the HTTP Headers cheat sheet, which currently only documents Access-Control-Allow-Origin.

The ACAO section lives in HTTP_Headers_Cheat_Sheet.md, so I would add the new subsection there, right after the existing Access-Control-Allow-Origin block. Please let me know if you would prefer it elsewhere.

My plan is a short subsection: Access-Control-Allow-Credentials must be the literal value true, it cannot be combined with Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * (browsers reject that pair), and setting it to true alongside a reflected or overly broad origin lets an attacker page read authenticated cross-origin responses. I would source it to the WHATWG Fetch Standard and the MDN page.

2946.title: Add Access-Control-Allow-Credentials to HTTP Headers Cheat Sheet
2946.body:
## Description

Adds documentation for the `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials` HTTP response header to the HTTP Headers Cheat Sheet.

The new subsection covers:
- The purpose and valid value of the header.
- Its relationship with `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` and the wildcard restriction.
- Security recommendations for trusted-origin validation.
- Cookie security considerations and CSRF protection.
- Credentialed CORS preflight behaviour.
